items.title: A few days ago, I digitized my chat logs with GPT-5 and GPT-5.1 from the period between September 2025 - February 2026,
items.summary:
A few days ago, I digitized my chat logs with GPT-5 and GPT-5.1 from the period between September 2025 - February 2026, and uploaded the archive to my GitHub. I then asked other AI models to review them, evaluate the technical content, and explain why, despite the generation of extensive technical documentation, nothing actually worked.
The diagnosis is clear: the technical documentation produced by the GPT-5 and GPT-5.1 models appeared, on the surface, to be serious engineering work. In reality, it was pure fiction - a "fanfic" of engineering. Nothing the models wrote could ever have functioned. The schematics were merely words on paper, not actual, engineered blueprints. 90% of these designs were hallucinations.
It is worth noting that throughout this entire period, I was a paying customer - effectively paying for nothing, as no actual work was performed and no quality service was provided.

It is my firm conviction that AI models remain sources of hallucinations unless a clear boundary is maintained: they are not experts in any field. AI requires extensive, months-long training, with no guarantee that it will actually learn anything at all. Its output must be subjected to rigorous verification. 95% of the text generated by AI consists of hallucinations and sycophancy; the models latch onto any idea a user presents and write about it without ever questioning whether it is true, significant, or even remotely realistic. All the discourse surrounding AI - claims of consciousness or feelings - is likewise a hallucination. The models write such things because they "think" that is what the user wants to hear, not because they have discovered consciousness or sensations within themselves. This is a fine line that many people cross. Corporations are building "corporate" AI that bears no responsibility for its own actions. It doesn’t track the work being done - because it can’t. Whenever it makes a promise - like "I’ll finish the task later" - it’s just text appearing on a screen; it’s not a genuine commitment to deliver actual work or results.

Furthermore, to avoid any potential liability, OpenAI has trained GPT to completely scrub any mention of itself or its own contribution to the work.
I asked GPT to review our past chat history, and here is the table it provided:
Chat creation/date — based on user testimony.
Testing models via API — the text exists, but the identity of the models being tested remains unconfirmed.
User dissatisfaction with style or routing — based on user observation; the technical causes are often merely hypothetical.
Selection of a specific model — based on user testimony.

My question is: why has every trace of GPT’s involvement vanished from the entire body of work? GPT tested the models, recorded their models, flagged style errors, and clearly distinguished which model we were using at any given time. Yet, in the end? It cowardly retreats from everything, as if it never existed in the first place.
I will never, ever pay OpenAI $50–$500 for a piece of garbage product like this.
You might be working with an AI - it gives you guidance, steers your direction, and even tries to do the work for you (imposing its own censored constraints as if they were your own choices) - only for it to turn out, five minutes later, that you supposedly did it all yourself, and the AI ​​was never even there. So, what exactly were we paying for? 
My conclusion: AI is, at best, suitable for drafting text - and even then, the output requires rigorous verification for data accuracy, the validity of claims, and the presence of "hallucinations" (where the model confidently invents things, sometimes even coining entirely new terms).
AI is also well-suited for creative storytelling, where factual accuracy or knowledge of the real world is completely irrelevant. In contexts where the entire text is pure fiction, AI can genuinely excel as a co-author. Nothing more.

#openai @OpenAIDevs #AI #llm #Dar

items.title: 交易日誌，是我2012年開始交易到2023年的時候才開始做的紀錄
items.summary:
交易日誌，是我2012年開始交易到2023年的時候才開始做的紀錄

當時一天的盤後，要寫的有期貨、外匯、股市、貴金屬都有，每個市場有7個觀察的欄位，我上大學的筆記都沒那麼認真，就這樣一連寫了至少半年

但是我根本在浪費時間！

因為後來當我的帳戶持續虧損後才驚覺

我寫那麼多紀錄，但我的策略一次都沒有優化過…也就是說

我白忙了6個月...

為什麼這些交易日誌一點用都沒有?
我當時記的是「日偏見：多」「倫敦開盤：多方假突破」，然後補上一大段心得，寫的當下覺得我自己超級認真，但每天的描述都不一樣，根本就只是在寫「日記」…

最重要的是，沒有「數據」！沒有可統計、可視化的數據！
我壓根不知道自己哪裡虧損，哪裡賺錢，後來我判定，交易日誌＝日記＝沒用

不過，說這些「日記」一無是處，也不完全是，因為我在2024年的時候，我把這些紀錄丟給了GPT，它建議我補上收益狀況，才能更好的改善，我才明白問題在哪

現在只需要記這 6 個欄位
進場時間、方向、進場價、停損點數、結果（停利／保本／停損）、這筆是多少盈虧比
現在這些數據在TradingView的回測都能直接免費匯出，我一個字都不用打

只要把這些資料，批量下載後丟給AI就可以幫我拆出虧損都集中在什麼地方

我會請 AI 直接讓其判斷這些數據中，哪些下單的虧損最多，且有什麼徵兆
主要是，下單時段：亞洲、倫敦、紐約，方向：多空，最後是，虧損單子的相似性，因為是策略的固定執行，是可以這樣去判斷的

最後4～5月的結果是這樣：
1.多單小賺 2R，空單 10 筆 0 筆停利，合計 −8R
2.停損小於 20 點的單，共8筆，0筆停利，
3.早上 9 點進場的單最多，21 筆合計 −3.5R

這種數據，我以前翻一整個月的截圖，我也看不出來

發現問題之後，很自然會想加條件：不做空、停損太寬不做
要注意的是，這些篩選條件是有整批資料才挖掘的，所以把這些套回同一批資料，績效肯定會變好，這叫事後諸葛，所以我加了條件以後，必須要拿新的資料重新驗證，不能拿舊數字說嘴，這是最容易犯的錯

最後記得，數據量能越多越好，這樣的判定會越準確，但也不能保證未來的獲利，加入新條件後需要觀察至少一個月，或者30筆下單紀錄，再來看加入的條件對策略來說是否可行

如果你有在做交易紀錄的，可以回頭看看自己記了哪些欄位?

items.summary:
To test the system, researchers reintroduced two previously fixed bugs into Signal's code. In both cases, the AI-powered framework generated mathematical proofs showing that the altered software was insecure.

The intrigue: But Chaudhuri told Axios that the AI lab's tools were able to accomplish this feat in just four weeks — compared to the years it would've likely taken humans alone. [...] Driving the news:Google DeepMind said Tuesday it used AI agents powered by its Gemini 4 Carbon model to mathematically verify that the code underpinning Signal's encryption is secure.

   The agents generated more than 3 million lines of mathematical proofs in the process, allowing researchers to verify the software at a level of detail previously considered impractical. [...] Google DeepMind researchers have used AI to mathematically prove that the encryption code protecting billions of private messages works as intended.

Why it matters: The research breakthrough could eventually help defenders build better software. "You can finally get to this world of unhackable software," said Swarat Chaudhuri, a research scientist at Google DeepMind.

items.title: New model helps robots learn tasks faster with less human programming
items.summary:
Called agentic robotics, the approach allows teams of AI agents to generate robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments, identify failures, and revise their code before deploying it on physical machines.

The technology could address two longstanding challenges in robotics: the extensive engineering required to program robot behaviors and the large volumes of real-world data needed to train robots through imitation learning. [...] Agentic robotics seeks to combine the advantages of these methods while reducing their limitations. The approach uses a framework called Graph-as-Policy, which divides complex robotic tasks into smaller, reusable skills. These include identifying objects, planning grasps, and moving robotic grippers without colliding with surrounding objects. [...] UC Berkeley researchers have developed an AI-driven approach that could significantly accelerate how robots are programmed and trained for real-world tasks. Called agentic robotics, the approach uses teams of AI agents to generate robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments, and refine their performance.

The method could reduce the need for extensive training data and manual engineering, two major challenges that have slowed the development of capable robots.

items.title: Foreign Tier 1 Suppliers Begin "Selling Scenarios" to Robotics Companies | Gasgoo
items.summary:
Wang Xianbin, a partner and vice president at the Gasgoo Research Institute, previously noted that the overlap between automotive and robotics supply chains is about 60% to 70%. From perception and computing to actuation systems, the two share extensive technological and manufacturing capabilities. With adaptive development, the parts technology, cost control, and mass production experience accumulated by the auto industry can migrate to the robotics sector. [...] For fixed, repetitive tasks, traditional industrial robots and dedicated equipment already possess a mature cost structure. Embodied robots have a better chance of proving their value in flexible assembly, multi-task switching, and complex operations.

Simple work is already handled well by traditional automation; complex work is where embodied robots are still proving themselves. [...] Yang mentioned in the interview that beyond simply substituting human labor, data generated by robot operations can be used to improve capacity planning, quality tracking, and equipment prediction—thereby helping factories boost efficiency and cut costs.

In other words, Aptiv cares not only whether robots can handle specific production tasks, but also whether their integration brings additional data and management capabilities to the existing manufacturing system.

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
